subject: Request: transient quota mitigation and structured true-up

Subject: sudden traffic spike — short-term capacity request

Hi Markus / Jordan,

We rolled a new clinical triage feature into canary last night and have an unexpected traffic spike. We expect sustained elevated inference volume for the next 10–14 days while we iterate on model prompts and throttles. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide temporary headroom (burst quota) and how billing would work?

- Current committed capacity: 2M tokens/day
- Peak expected: ~4.5M tokens/day for ~10 days
- Immediate need: ability to avoid hard throttles and keep live tests running

I've attached recent request metrics (omni_surge_metrics.csv). Procurement may need an estimated invoice impact to approve.

Thanks,
Elena

Folks — forwarding OmniHealth's note. They need immediate headroom and a clear billing path for procurement. High level thoughts:

Options we can present quickly (fastest to implement first):
1) Soft burst window: enable +50% capacity for up to 7 days with overrun billed at pay-as-you-go rate (no contract).
2) Bridge commit: 30-day provisional commit (prorated), 20% discount on the incremental units for the period, with a true-up invoice at period end. Credit applied to next invoice.
3) Emergency credit: one-off goodwill credit to cover part of the overrun while product team stabilizes (requires AE + finance sign-off).

Rachel — can you confirm how a bridge commit true-up and one-off credit would flow in our billing system? Also need max activation lead time if we flip the routing/policy.

I want to give Elena two concrete choices and an estimated delta they can send to procurement.

-Markus
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the CSV. Quick clarification items so we can size the offer:
- Can you confirm average tokens/second at peak and whether the traffic is evenly spread or a few hot endpoints?
- Do you want headroom only (keep current commit + temporary capacity) or are you open to a short-term provisional commit?

Two concrete proposals to accelerate procurement:
A) Soft burst window (fast):
- Duration: up to 7 calendar days
- Headroom: +50% of existing commit
- Billing: overrun billed at PAYG rate (no discount), visible in Console under route usage
- Activation: same-day if requested before 2pm PT

B) 30-day bridge commit (recommended for predictable cost):
- Duration: 30 days starting on activation date
- Incremental commit: add 60% of current commit for the period (pro-rated)
- Pricing: 20% discount on incremental units for the 30-day window
- Billing: prorated invoice at next billing cycle, true-up at period close; one-time credit applied if invoice over-assesses
- Activation: requires signed confirmation (DocuSign) + finance acceptance; target turnaround 24–48 hours

I've attached a short pricing workbook with line items for both options (redwood_pricing_bridge_workbook.xlsx). If you want the fastest path, we can enable A immediately and follow with B if procurement prefers a structured short commit.

DocuSign link for the provisional commit (if you pick B): https://www.docusign.com/sign/placeholder-link-for-bridge-commit

-Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Elena / team — quick finance note on the Bridge commit (option B):
- Activation & invoicing: we can activate within ~24 hours after we receive a signed confirmation.
- Prorated charge: the incremental commit will be prorated for the active days in the billing period and appear on the next invoice.
- True-up: at the end of the 30-day window we run a reconciliation. If they used less than the provisional commit, we issue a one-time credit to the invoice that closes the window. If they used more, the overrun is billed at the agreed incremental rate.
- Credits & accounting: one-off credits are posted as invoice adjustments (they are not applied as refunds).

Attached is a template we use to show the estimated invoice delta for procurement (bridge_commit_invoice_template.pdf). Jordan: tell me which numbers you want me to populate (best/expected/worst) and I can send the summary to Elena's procurement contact.

-Rachel
Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
